name: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav Attack
summary: The Yugoslav Attack (Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O) is White’s critical anti-Dragon try, castling long to storm the kingside with h4-h5.
intro: The Yugoslav Attack is the main test of the Sicilian Dragon, reached after 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Be3 Bg7 7.f3 O-O 8.Qd2 Nc6. White sets up Be3, f3 and Qd2, castles queenside, and races to open Black’s king with h4-h5 and g4, while Black counterattacks down the half-open c-file.
line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The Yugoslav Attack produces one of the sharpest strategic pictures in all of chess: opposite-side castling and a naked race between two attacks. White’s formation of Be3, f3 and Qd2 supports the plan of castling queenside and then throwing the h- and g-pawns forward to prise open lines against the fianchettoed king. The move f3 does double duty, shoring up e4 and preparing g4, while the dark-squared bishop and queen line up for sacrifices on the kingside, above all the thematic exchange of White’s dark-squared bishop for the Dragon bishop on g7.

Black’s counterplay is equally direct and flows down the c-file. The rook swings to c8, the knight often reroutes via e5 to c4 to hit the queen and dark squares, and Black looks for the celebrated exchange sacrifice ...Rxc3, smashing White’s queenside pawn shield and exposing the king on c1. The position is a genuine race in which tempo is everything: whoever lands the decisive blow first usually wins outright, and both sides must know precisely which pawn to push and which piece to sacrifice at each turn.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: White’s two principal set-ups after castling long are the lines with 9.Bc4, the Soltis and related systems, and the direct 9.O-O-O followed by an immediate pawn storm. With 9.Bc4 White places the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal to restrain ...d5 and control key light squares before advancing on the wing; with the plain 9.O-O-O Black frequently strikes back with the freeing central break ...d5 to blunt the attack. Understanding when ...d5 equalises and when it fails is one of the central questions of Dragon theory.

The most heavily analysed battleground features the exchange sacrifice ...Rxc3, met by bxc3, after which Black continues to unravel White’s king position while White pushes h4-h5 and prepares to open the h-file. Long forcing sequences arise involving the trade of dark-squared bishops via Bh6, the knight raid ...Nc4, and races where each side’s attack hangs by a single tempo. Because so much is forced, the Yugoslav Attack rewards deep home preparation more than almost any other Sicilian.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The Yugoslav Attack takes its name from the strong Yugoslav masters who developed the queenside-castling plan in the mid-twentieth century, and it rapidly became the acid test of the Dragon. Its reputation as a mutual mating race was captured by Bobby Fischer, who summarised the White plan against the Dragon with the memorable phrase about opening the h-file, sacrificing, and delivering mate. The line was a battleground in many World Championship-era preparations and remains a favourite of aggressive players who relish opposite-side castling. Theory continues to evolve, but its essential character of all-out attack against all-out counterattack has never changed.

keyIdeas: Opposite-side castling turns the game into a direct race to mate.
White’s Be3, f3, Qd2 set-up prepares O-O-O and an h4-h5 pawn storm.
Trading the dark-squared bishops with Bh6 strips Black’s king of its defender.
Black’s counterplay runs down the half-open c-file with ...Rc8 and ...Nc4.
The exchange sacrifice ...Rxc3 shatters White’s queenside pawn cover.
The central break ...d5 can defuse the attack when White castles without Bc4.

white: Castle queenside and launch the h- and g-pawns at Black’s king.
Play Bc4 to restrain ...d5 and control the light squares before attacking.
Exchange dark-squared bishops via Bh6 to weaken g7 and the dark squares.
Open the h-file with h4-h5xg6 and double heavy pieces against h7.
Calculate the mating race precisely, sacrificing to gain the decisive tempo.
black: Occupy the c-file with ...Rc8 and pressure the c3-knight.
Reroute a knight to c4 to hit the queen and White’s dark squares.
Sacrifice the exchange with ...Rxc3 to demolish White’s queenside pawns.
Seek the freeing ...d5 break to blunt White’s central and kingside power.
Win the race by exposing the c1-king one tempo ahead of White.
